# rezip_files

[← Command index](README.md)

Rebuild zip files in place with fixed, reproducible 7-Zip settings.

## Synopsis

```
rezip_files [options]
```

## Description

Finds every `.zip` file under the input path (or takes the one file given) and
rebuilds it with 7-Zip: the zip is extracted to a `<name>_extracted` folder beside it
and deleted, then the folder's contents are zipped back to the original path and the
folder is deleted.

The new zip uses Deflate at level 7, leaves out NTFS timestamps, stores non-ASCII
names as UTF-8 and asks 7-Zip for a reproducible archive.

The run stops with an error at the first zip that cannot be extracted or rebuilt.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | A `.zip` file, or a directory searched recursively for them; must exist. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Rebuild every zip in a folder

```bash
rezip_files -i /path/to/zips
```

### Rebuild one zip without the confirmation prompt

```bash
rezip_files -i "/path/to/Game (USA).zip" --no-preview
```

## Notes

- The original zip is deleted before the new one is written. If the rebuild fails, the files are still in the `<name>_extracted` folder.
- Each zip is extracted in full next to itself, so that directory needs room for its uncompressed contents.
- 7-Zip must be installed as a JoyBox tool.
